Dabrowa Tarnowska Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dąbrowa Tarnowska, Poland

Not demolished. Dąbrowa Tarnowska was the center of the Dombrov Hasidic dynasty from the 19th century; several of its leaders are buried in this cemetery, including Mordechaj Dawid Unger (died 1843), Josef Unger (died 1876), and Mosze Eliakim Unger (died 1917). On July 22, 1942, the Germans shot about 180 local Jews at the cemetery, using it as an execution ground; tombstones were subsequently used to pave the courtyard of Wehrmacht headquarters and town roads, and to build a swimming pool. In 1991, the ohel was rebuilt through the efforts of Rabbi Mendl Reichberg, and in 1992 Jewish immigrants from Dąbrowa Tarnowska re-fenced the cemetery. The last burials took place in 1994 and 1995.
